zikiltum: UNCERTAIN: folly, the part of a fool (Harper “the part of a fool”; his glossary files it as šikiltu, though his text spells zi-): zikiltam (zi-ki-il-tam, accusative), set beside the verb zakālum of the same root; the pair is Harper’s sense and UNCERTAIN by later standards
zakālum: UNCERTAIN: to play the fool (Harper): izakkil (i-za-ak-ki-il, present, 3rd person), used with the noun zikiltum of the same root; the sense rests on Harper’s glossary, which files the verb as šakālu “to play the part of a fool”
sapāḫum-D: D-stem of sapāḫum “to scatter”: to scatter, neglect (Harper: “to scatter, to neglect”), said of a house or household: uzappaḫ (u-za-ap-pa-aḫ, present, 3rd person)
maṭûm-Š: Š-stem of maṭûm “to be small”: to make small, belittle (Harper: “to make little, to belittle”): ušamṭa (u-ša-am-ṭa, present, 3rd person, read as ušamṭâ: the present of a Š-stem of a verb ending in a vowel ends in -â, the preterite in -i), ušamṭaši (u-ša-am-ṭa-ši) “he belittles her”, with -ši “her”; Harper prints the sign as da, read ṭa; the exact vowel is UNCERTAIN
-anni: me (1st-person singular accusative suffix, on a verb; the ventive -am + -ni): taḫḫazanni (ta-aḫ-ḫa-za-an-ni) “you take me”
parāsum-N: N-stem (passive) of parāsum “to decide”: ipparrasma (ip-pa-ar-ra-aš-ma, present with -ma) “it shall be decided, and”; the present without -ma is ipparras “it shall be decided”
ḫiṭītum: UNCERTAIN: sin, fault, defect: ḫiṭītam (ḫi-ṭi-tam, accusative); Harper prints ḫi-di-tam, but the middle sign DI also reads ṭi, and his glossary does not list the word, so the identification rests on the sign reading and the context
erēbum-Š: Š-stem of erēbum “to enter”: to make enter, bring in: ušērribši (u-še-ir-ri-ib-ši) “he shall bring her in”, with -ši “her”
maḫārum-Št: UNCERTAIN: Št-stem of maḫārum “to face, be level with”, reflexive: to make oneself equal to (Harper: III,2, “to take precedence of”): uštamaḫḫar (uš-ta-ma-aḫ-ḫa-ar, present) and uštatamḫir (uš-ta-tam-ḫi-ir, perfect, with the t of the perfect after the stem’s š); the exact nuance is not secure
bēltum: lady, mistress (the feminine of bēlum): bēltiša (be-el-ti-ša) “her mistress”; bēlissa (be-li-za) “her mistress”, from the construct bēlit + -ša, t + š said ss
abbuttum: UNCERTAIN: Harper “service, slavery”; later dictionaries read a mark of slavery: abbuttam (ab-bu-ut-tam, accusative), used with šakānum “to set, impose” (abbuttam išakkan); the sense is not secure
laʾbum: UNCERTAIN: a sickness, disease (Harper “fever, disease”): laʾbum (la-a-bu-um, nominative); what illness is meant is not known
baqārum: to claim, make a claim against (Harper: BAKARU “to make claim”): ibaqqarūši (i-ba-qa₂-ru-ši, present plural, “they shall claim against her”) with -ši “her”; Harper prints the sign as ga, read qa₂
râmum: to love: irammu (i-ra-am-mu, present), with the subjunctive -u after ša: ša irammu “whom he/she loves”
rakāsum-D: D-stem of rakāsum “to bind”: to bind (by agreement), contract with (Harper: “to contract with”): urtakkis (ur-ta-ak-ki-is, perfect, with the t of the perfect after the first sign); who the subject is rests on the context
ezēbum-Š: UNCERTAIN: Š-stem of ezēbum “to leave”: to have left, have deposited (a document): uštēzib (uš-te-zi-ib, perfect, 3rd person); the Š-stem šūzubum elsewhere means “to save, rescue”, so the sense with a tablet (ṭuppam uštēzib) rests on the context
lāma: before (la-ma), as a conjunction with a verb in the subjunctive: lāma … iḫḫazu “before he takes”
kilallān: both (of two): kilallašunu (ki-la-la-šu-nu) “both of them”, with -šunu “their, of them”

__broaden__.-ša: her / its (3rd-person feminine suffix) · on nouns, “her”: after a t the š is assimilated and said ss, spelled with the sign ZA: bīssa (bi-za, or É-za) “her house”, mussa (mu-za) “her husband”, warkassa (wa-ar-ka-za) “her case”, bēlissa (be-li-za) “her mistress”; otherwise written plainly: panīša, mutiša, abiša, šeriqtaša, bēltiša · on an infinitive, the object “her”: ṣabātiša “seizing her” · on a verb-like form: ezibša (e-zi-ib-ša, UNCERTAIN in form) · on a plural noun: mārūša (DUMU{meš}-ša) “her sons”
__broaden__.-šu: his / him · -šum “to him, for him” (dative): išakkanūšum, innadnušum · after a dental the suffix is assimilated and spelled with z: …ssu (ṣibat-zu, ṣibassu “its interest”, written after a broken sign); with a noun: ṣibtišu “its interest”, qātīšu “his hand”, damqaršu “his merchant”; tu-šu, te-šu in broken forms · with the same assimilation after a t: aššassu (aš-ša-zu) “his wife”, from aššat + -šu, t + š said ss · on a verb, the object “him”, or “to him” in the dative (Harper writes -šu for -šum): imaggarūšu (i-ma-ag-ga-ru-šu) “they shall agree to him”; on a noun after a preposition: elišu “upon him”
__broaden__.-ši: her / it (3rd-person feminine singular suffix, on a verb): ukannūšima “they shall convict her”, inaddûši “they shall throw her”, iqallûši “they shall burn her” · iṣṣabassi (iṣ-ṣa-ba-az-zi) “it has seized her” (the t of the perfect + -ši said ss, spelled -zi) · on the present plural: imannûši “they shall count her”, ibaqqarūši “they shall claim against her” · on the Š-stem: ušērribši “he shall bring her in”, ušamṭaši “he has belittled her”
__broaden__.ezēbum: to leave; Š-stem šūzubum: ušēzib “he deposited (a document)” · īzib (preterite) “he left (over)” · to leave, divorce: izzibši (i-iz-zi-ib-ši, present, “he shall divorce her”) · ezibša (e-zi-ib-ša) “(I) divorce her”, a quoted word, UNCERTAIN in form (the object “her” on a verb is normally -ši) · īzibšim (i-zi-ib-ši-im, preterite) “he left to her”, said of a deed or gift left to someone
__broaden__.waṣûm: to go out; ūṣiamma “he came forward” · wuṣîm (wa-ṣi-im, the infinitive wuṣûm in the genitive after ana) “to go out” · waṣīma (wa-ṣi-ma, with -ma) and waṣiat (wa-ṣi-a-at, stative 3rd feminine) “going out”; the PI sign reads wa or wu, ZI is read ṣi, and the nuance of the form is UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.pānum: front, face: ina pani “in front of” · panīša ištakan “she has set her face”: the idiom for making up one’s mind, resolving to do something; with ana + infinitive “to …” (panīšu, panīša “his, her face”)
__broaden__.šakānum: to set, place: išakkanūšumma “they shall set for him (a term), and” · išakkanūšum (present, plural, dative -šum) “they shall place (it) for him”, i.e. count it to him · iššakkan (iš-ša-ak-ka-an, N-stem present) “it shall be put”: ul iššakkan “it shall not be put (in the account)” · to set, put, impose: ištakan (iš-ta-ka-an, perfect, “has set”), išakkan (present) — išakkanšima (i-ša-ak-ka-an-ši-ma, with -ši and -ma) “he/she shall set (it) on her, and”, as in abbuttam išakkan
__broaden__.wašābum: to sit: ul uššab “he shall not sit” (the stone writes uš-ta-ab — a carver’s slip Harper flags) · to dwell: wāšbum (participle, contracted) “the dweller, the tenant” (a conjectured reading, aš-bu-u[m]); wa… “dwell-” in broken forms · stative wašbat (wa-aš-ba-at) “she dwells, lives”: ša ina gagîm lā wašbat “who does not live in the cloister” · stative wašib (wa-ši-ib-ma, with -ma) “he is staying”: ina ḫarrānim wašib “he is staying on the road” · present uššab “she shall live” (uš-ša-ab) and uššamma (uš-ša-am-ma, the b becoming m before -ma) · infinitive wašābam (wa-ša-ba-am) “to live”, in the accusative after a verb
__broaden__.aḫāzum: to take, grasp; Š-stem šūḫuzum “to make take hold” · to take (a wife): iḫuz (i-ḫu-uz) preterite, iḫuzma “he took, and”; present iḫḫaz (i-iḫ-ḫa-az) “he shall take”, which also serves as a permission, “he may take”; iḫḫazu (i-iḫ-ḫa-zu, with the subjunctive -u) “(before) he takes”; infinitive aḫāzim (a-ḫa-zi-im), taking its object in the genitive; taḫḫazanni (2nd person, with -anni “me”)
__broaden__.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …” · iddin, iddinu “he gave” (preterite; the subjunctive -u in a ša- or inūma clause); iddinma “he gave, and”; …in, …din in broken forms; inaddin “he shall give”: ana damqaršu inaddin “he shall give to his merchant” · ittadinma (it-ta-di-in-ma) “he has given, and” (perfect); inaddinu (i-na-ad-di-nu) “(which) he gives” (present, with the subjunctive -u) · ittandin (it-ta-an-di-in, perfect with an extra -n-) “he has handed over”: ana kiššātim ittandin “he handed over into service”; ittadin (it-ta-din) “he has given”, i.e. sold; ana maṣṣarūtim inaddin “he gives for safekeeping”; iddinūšumma “they gave him, and” · inaddin also of a woman, “she shall give” · inaddišši (i-na-ad-di-iš-ši) “he/she shall give her” (the n of the stem swallowed before -ši), of a sale: ana kaspim inaddišši “she may sell her”, ul inaddišši “she shall not sell her”
__broaden__.ṣabātum: to seize: iṣṣabat, ṣabtu · stative with the subjunctive -u: adi kirâm ṣabtu “as long as he holds the orchard” (with Harper’s kirûm: “as long as the orchard is held”) · iṣṣabtamma (iṣ-ṣa-ab-tam-ma) “she seized (them), and” (perfect with the ventive -am and -ma): lā iṣṣabtamma “and she did not seize” · iṣbassuma (iṣ-ba-zu-ma, ZU for -ssu) “it seized him, and” (preterite iṣbat + -šu + -ma), of a debt seizing a man · iṣṣabtūšu (iṣ-ṣa-ab-tu-šu) “they seized him” (perfect, plural, with -šu “him”); iṣṣabat (iṣ-ṣa-ba-at) “he has seized (his wife)” (perfect) · iṣṣabassi (iṣ-ṣa-ba-az-zi) “it has seized her” (perfect + -ši, t + š said ss); present plural iṣabbatū (i-ṣa-ba-tu) “they shall seize”; preterite with the subjunctive iṣbatu; infinitive with suffix ṣabātiša “seizing her”
__broaden__.bašûm: to exist, arise: ibbaššû “which arose” · lā ibaššišum “there is not to him” (= he has none), with dative -šum · in broken forms …ši (ul ibašši, “there is not”, the verb itself restored); ibaššû “which are (there)”, in mimma ina qātīšu ibaššû · ibašši (i-ba-aš-ši, present) “there is, is upon”: ḫubullum elišu ibašši “a debt is upon him”
__broaden__.erēbum: to enter: iterub “she has entered” (perfect; Harper I,2) · irrubu (i-ir-ru-bu) “she enters” and īrubu (i-ru-bu) “she entered” — present and preterite with the subjunctive -u, after lāma “before” and ištu “after”
__broaden__.walādum: to bear, give birth to: ūlidušum (ul-du-šum) “(whom) she bore to him” (preterite ūlid, the long ū of a w-initial verb, with the subjunctive -u and the dative -šum; Harper’s spelling is shortened, so the vowels of the form are UNCERTAIN) · ittalad (it-ta-la-ad, perfect) “she has borne” · ūlid (u-li-id, preterite) “she bore”, ūldu (ul-du, with subjunctive -u)
__broaden__.mārum: son (DUMU) — here: a minor, not yet able to sell · member of a group: mārū ugārim (DUMU A.GÀR{meš}) “the sons of the irrigated land”, the district’s farmers · mār awīlim “a man’s son” (DUMU); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons” (oblique plural, which may include daughters, so “children”); māršu (DUMU-šu) “his son” · mārūša (DUMU{meš}-ša) “her sons” (nominative plural + suffix); mārīša (DUMU-ša) “her son” (genitive + suffix): ana mārīša “to her son”
__broaden__.amtum: slave-woman (GEME₂) · amassu (GEME₂-zu) “his slave-woman”, amtam (GEME₂-am), amtim (GEME₂-tim) · plural amâti (GEME₂{meš}) “slave-women”; the exact plural signs are UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.aššatum: wife: ana aššatišu “to his wife” · aššassu (SAL-zu, ZU for -ssu) “his wife” · construct aššat (aš-ša-at) “wife of” before a genitive: aššat awīlim · aššatam, aššatim, aššatum, written SAL (the same sign as zinništum “woman”) or aš-ša-tam
__broaden__.šanûm: another, a second one: ana šanîm “to another”, šanûm “another man” · feminine šanītum “another (woman)”: šanītam, šanītim (ša-ni-tam, ša-ni-tim), in the accusative and genitive
__broaden__.eli: against, upon · with suffixes: elišu, eliša, elišunu “upon him, her, them” (of a debt)
__broaden__.magārum: to agree, consent: imtagarma (perfect, with -ma) “has come to an agreement”, said of a settlement made with another party (itti …) · imaggarūšu (i-ma-ag-ga-ru-šu, present plural + -šu) “they shall agree to him” · imtagar (im-ta-gar, perfect) “she has agreed” (ana + infinitive)
__broaden__.balāṭum: to live; D-stem bulluṭum — muballiṭ “who gives life” · stative baltat (ba-al-ṭa-at) “she lives”, in adi baltat “as long as she lives”
__broaden__.našûm: to bear, carry: ittanašši “he shall bear (the penalty)” · našû (na-šu-u, stative with the subjunctive -u) “(that) he carried”: mimma ša našû “anything that he carried” · ittanaššiši (it-ta-na-aš-ši-ši, Gtn present + -ši) “he shall keep carrying (supporting) her”
__broaden__.epēšum: to do, make: epēšim “doing” · to work (land): ippeš(ma) (present): eqlam šipram ippeš “he shall do the work on the field” · to build (?) (a house): bītam ippēšma(?) “he builds a house, and”, the verb broken; iteppuš (?) in a broken line · ippešū (i-ib-bi-šu) “they shall do (work), they shall work” (present plural) · īpušu (i-pu-šu, preterite with the subjunctive -u) “(which) he built”: to make, build (a house)
__broaden__.bēlum: owner, lord: bēl ḫulqim “owner of the lost property” · owner of a field, bēl eqlim; bēl ḫubullim “creditor” · bēl kirîm “owner of the orchard” · bēl (be-el), the construct “owner of”, also with a suffix on the noun that follows: bēl ḫubullišu “his creditor”, bēl ḫubulliša “her creditor”
__broaden__.ḫarrānum: road; campaign: ḫarrān šarrim “the king’s campaign” (spelled ḫar-ra-an, or carved with the road-sign KASKAL) · journey, the merchant’s trading trip: ana ḫarrānim “on a journey” (the editors print ḫarranim; the spelling ḫar-ra-nim is uncertain here), ina ḫarrānim “on the journey” · UNCERTAIN: Harper “way, road, journey, errand”: ḫarrānša (ḫa-ra-an-ša) “her journey”, a payment she does not get — a guess at a travel-allowance (Harper’s own translation: “on her departure”)
__broaden__.warkatum: the circumstances, the facts of the case: warkassu “his case” (warkat + šu, t+š → ss) · UNCERTAIN: warkassa (wa-ar-ka-za) “her case” (what is examined and decided) and “her estate” (what she leaves behind), the second reading resting on the context
__broaden__.alākum: to go: illak “he shall go” · illiku “(where) he went” (preterite, subjunctive -u, after a restored ašar), in the agent law · alākišu (a-la-ki-šu) “his going” (infinitive with -šu): ina alākišu “in his going” · Gt present ittallak (it-ta-al-la-ak) “she shall go away” (the Gt gives the sense of going off; the Gtn would be ittanallak)
__broaden__.aššum: because (of); concerning · because; with a clause, also “so that”, giving purpose or reason (aššum … lā ṣabātiša, UNCERTAIN in grammar)
__broaden__.bītum: house, estate · bīt karānim “wine-house, tavern” (construct form bīt, written É); bītiša “her house” (É-ša) · bīt awīlim “a man’s house”; bīssa (bi-za, É-za) “her house”, written with É or syllabically with BI + ZA; bītišu (É-šu) “his house”; genitive bītim, accusative bītam, written É alone
